eps.o: Kylie and Dannii Minogue voice Bluey and Bingo in a heartwarming tale of self-discovery and sisterly affection. Bluey devises a plan to become more like Bingo after their dad, Bandit, complains about how dissimilar they are. After colouring Bingo in blue chalk, Bluey happily introduces Mini Bluey!

BINDI IRWIN narrates The Creek, a story about learning not to be scared of nature and seeing the beauty of the wild world outside. When Bluey is bored at the park Mackenzie suggests a trip to the creek. Bluey is unsure as she has never been there before – what will she find when she explores the creek?

TOM DALEY narrates Barky Boats, a story about what happens when we need to prepare for a big new adventure. Bluey wants to make a fairy garden with her buddy Mia, but Mackenzie wants to play barky boats with his buddy Captain. When the buddies run off to play together, Calypso steps in to help Bluey and Mackenzie understand why…

ROMESH RANGANATHAN narrates ‘Easter', a story about patience and remembering that we're rememberable! Bluey and Bingo are worried that the Easter bunny will forget about them. On Easter morning, a series of clues are left for them to solve throughout the house, but will they be able to find the chocolate eggs?

Suranne Jones reads ‘Grannies', featuring everyones favourite Nanas: Janet and Rita! Bluey and Bingo are having lots of fun playing Grannies in the kitchen. Bingo thinks than grannies can floss, but Bluey disagrees. Mum and Dad are no help either, so they call their real-life Nana to answer their question…

JENNA FISCHER narrates Charades. Bluey, Bingo, Muffin, and Socks are staying at Nana's and decide to play a game of charades. Muffin, however, doesn't quite understand the rules! Bluey and Bingo wonder why they have to play along, but there's only one important rule to remember when you're at Nana's house: you get what you want!

Eva Mendes narrates Mum School. Bluey wants Mum to grade her on her parenting skills as she attempts to parent five bouncy balloons, but one named Greenie proves tricky to handle! After observing Dad parent Bingo, Bluey finally knows how to treat Greenie right…

Jordan Fisher narrates Swim School. Bluey is playing two swim school teachers: Karen and (the much meaner) Margaret! Mum, Dad, and Bingo reckon they can pass Margaret's Big Fish classes without dobbing on each other, but it's proving to be quite the challenge…

Camille Cottin narrates ‘The Beach', a story about Bluey embarking on a solo quest across the shoreline! When mum goes for a walk by herself along the beach, Bluey runs to catch up with her, keen to share a shell she has found. Pretending to be a mermaid who has finally got her legs for the day, she embarks on a precious solo adventure, following Mum's footprints along the shoreline.

Rob Delaney narrates ‘Daddy Putdown', a story about Bluey learning to play and have fun when Mum is away. Mum has to go to a baby shower, but Bluey misses her and wants her to come back! To cheer Bluey up, Dad thinks of some games to distract her…

It's Christmas Eve and Bluey, Bingo, Muffin and Socks can't wait to open their presents. But Bluey's dad reminds them that no peeking or no presents! So, they decide to play a game called Verandah Santa to practice no peeking. What will Santa bring them? A Bluey Christmas story, Read by Adam Hills.

Ian Thorpe narrates Christmas Swim, a story about giving new families a chance (even if they are a bit crazy!). On Christmas Morning, Bluey opens a present containing a brand new teddy: Bartlebee! However, it all becomes slightly too much for him after the Heelers end up breaking his arm. Bluey tells Frisky he wants to go home, what will she say to convince him to stay?
